originality.rationale: The 2024 primary paper provides all intact Petersen maximal general-position facets, a strong covering result for intact counting but not for shortest-path relations after a graph fault. The new claims require fresh recomputation of the altered metric and an exact homotopy reduction: edge deletion yields a new circle plus three 2-spheres, whereas vertex deletion gives two 2-spheres. Searches against primary literature, aliases, nearby graph families and an indexed mathematical-results collection revealed no theorem implying these two fault homotopy types; residual risk of unindexed equivalent work is explicitly retained.

value.rationale: The Petersen graph is a canonical edge- and vertex-transitive distance-regular example with an explicit general-position facet census already in the literature. Determining the topology after deletion is a natural graph-metric robustness problem, not a variant obtained by deleting a face of the old simplicial complex. The edge fault changes simply connected intact S³ into a space with fundamental group Z and three independent 2-sphere summands, while vertex fault gives a simply connected two-sphere wedge. The contrast is a motivated first-fault classification with exact integral homotopy, not merely a face-count update.
